html:
The last emperor of China, who took the Qing throne in 1908 at the age of two and was forced to give it up in 1912. His life ran from the Forbidden City to a communist prison to a quiet job in Beijing.

Cixi chose him as heir on her deathbed. He reigned as the Xuantong Emperor until the Xinhai Revolution ended the empire. Under the abdication terms he kept his title and lived on in the Forbidden City. A general restored him to the throne for twelve days in 1917. In 1924 he was expelled and moved to the Japanese concession in Tianjin.

Japan, having seized Manchuria, made him head of its puppet state of Manchukuo in 1932, and emperor in 1934. He had little real power. In 1945 Soviet troops captured him, and in 1950 he was handed to the new People's Republic. After nearly ten years of re-education he was pardoned in 1959 and worked as a gardener and an archive editor. He died in 1967. The 1987 film The Last Emperor told his story.
